title: Chapter 11. THEY MEET THE WOODEN GARGOYLES
chineseTitle: 第11章 他们遇见木制石像鬼

paragraphs.en: The adventurers reached a third landing where a rift in the mountain offered a view of thick clouds. The Wizard produced nine tiny piglets from his pocket; they were now visible, proving their exit from the Valley of Voe's magical influence.
paragraphs.zh: 冒险者们来到了第三个休息平台，只见山体裂开了一道缝隙，露出了浓厚的云雾。巫师从口袋里掏出九只小猪仔；它们现在清晰可见，证明他们已经脱离了沃谷魔法的影响。

paragraphs.en: "Look, we can see each other again!" exclaimed one piglet joyfully.
paragraphs.zh: “看，我们又能互相看见了！”小猪高兴地喊道。

paragraphs.en: "Yes," sighed Eureka, "and I'm starving. May I have just one of these little pigs? You wouldn't miss it."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”尤里卡叹了口气，“我还饿着呢。我可以吃一个这样的小香肠吗？你不会介意的。”

paragraphs.en: "What a savage creature!" cried another piglet. "We've been such good friends and played together!"
paragraphs.zh: “真是个野蛮的家伙！”另一只小猪喊道，“我们可是好伙伴，还经常一起玩啊！”

paragraphs.en: "When my stomach isn't empty, I love to play with you all," said the kitten demurely. "But when hungry, nothing fills me like a fat piglet."
paragraphs.zh: “当我肚子不饿的时候，我很喜欢和你们一起玩，”小猫娇滴滴地说，“可是饿起来的时候，没有什么能比一只肥嘟嘟的小猪崽更让我满足了。”

paragraphs.en: "And we trusted you so!" said one of the nine, reproachfully.
paragraphs.zh: “我们竟然这么信任你！”其中一人愤慨地说。

paragraphs.en: "And thought you were respectable!" added another.
paragraphs.zh: “原来你还有点规矩！”另一个人加了一句。

paragraphs.en: "It seems we were mistaken," declared a third, looking at the kitten fearfully. "No one with such murderous desires should be in our party."
paragraphs.zh: “看来我们搞错了，”第三个成员战战兢兢地说道，“像有如此杀机的人不该出现在我们的队伍里。”

paragraphs.en: "You see, Eureka," Dorothy reprimanded, "you're making yourself disliked. There are proper things for kittens to eat, but never a pig under any circumstances."
paragraphs.zh: “你看，尤里卡，”多萝西责备道，“你这样会让自己变得不讨人喜欢的。小猫应该吃合适的食物，绝不能让猪来凑这个热闹。”

paragraphs.en: "Did you ever see such little pigs?" asked the kitten. "They're no bigger than mice, and I'm sure they're proper for me to eat."
paragraphs.zh: “你见过这么小的猪没？”小猫问道，“它们比老鼠还小，我肯定可以吃掉它们。”

paragraphs.en: "It isn't about size; it's variety," replied Dorothy. "These are Mr. Wizard's pets, just like you're my pet. It wouldn't be proper for you to eat them any more than Jim should eat you."
paragraphs.zh: “这不在于体型，而在于多样性，”多萝西回答说，“这些是巫师先生的宠物，就像你是我的宠物一样。你吃它们也不比吉姆吃你更合适。”

paragraphs.en: "If you don't leave those little pork balls alone, I'll chew you up instantly," warned Jim, glaring at the kitten with his round eyes.
paragraphs.zh: “如果你不停手，我立刻会把你嚼得粉碎。”吉姆瞪大眼睛警告着那只小猫，语气中透出不容置疑的威胁。

paragraphs.en: The kitten considered Jim thoughtfully. "In that case," she said, "I'll leave them alone. You haven't many teeth left, but they're sharp enough to make me shudder.
paragraphs.zh: 小猫认真地想了想，对吉姆说道：“既然这样，”她说，“我还是让他们独自待着吧。你剩下的牙齿不多了，但它们锋利得很，让我都不寒而栗。”

paragraphs.en: So the piglets will be safe from me."
paragraphs.zh: “这样一来，小猪们就安全了。”

paragraphs.en: Eureka yawned and stretched. "I've always loved the piglets," she said, "but they don't love me." Dorothy replied, "No one can love a person he's afraid of.
paragraphs.zh: 欧瑞卡打了个哈欠，伸了伸懒腰。“我一直喜欢小猪崽们，”她说，“但他们并不喜欢我。”多萝西回答道：“任何人如果害怕一个人，都不会爱他。”

paragraphs.en: If you behave, I'm sure the little pigs will grow fond of you."
paragraphs.zh: 如果你乖一点，小猪们肯定会喜欢上你的。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard placed the nine tiny piglets back in his pocket and resumed their journey up the dark, winding stairway. "We must be near the top," said Jim. Dorothy added, "The Country of the Gurgles can't be far from the top of the earth.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师把九只小猪仔又放回口袋里，继续沿着幽暗蜿蜒的楼梯向上攀登。“我们快到顶了。”吉姆说道。多萝西也补充说：“咕噜国应该就在地表的顶端不远了。”

paragraphs.en: It isn't very nice down here; I'd like to get home."
paragraphs.zh: 这里不太舒服；我想回家。

paragraphs.en: As they climbed, the stairs narrowed, and Zeb and the Wizard had to help pull the buggy up or prevent it from jamming against the rocky walls. Finally, a dim light appeared ahead, growing clearer as they approached.
paragraphs.zh: 随着他们攀爬，楼梯逐渐变窄，泽布和巫师不得不帮忙拉拽马车，以免它被卡在岩石壁上。终于，在他们靠近时，前方出现了一丝微弱的光线，渐渐变得明亮起来。

paragraphs.en: "Thank goodness we're nearly there!" panted the little Wizard. Jim, leading the way, saw the last stair and stuck his head out.
paragraphs.zh: “谢天谢地，我们快到了！”小巫师喘着气说道。吉姆走在前面，看见了最后一级台阶，探出头来。

paragraphs.en: He then ducked down, nearly falling with the buggy onto the others. "Let's go back down," he said hoarsely.
paragraphs.zh: 他随即蹲下身子， buggy 差点翻倒在他身旁。“我们回去吧，”他嘶哑着嗓子说道。

paragraphs.en: "Nonsense!" snapped the tired Wizard. "What's wrong with you, old man?"
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道！”疲惫的巫师脱口而出，“你这老头怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: "Everything," grumbled Jim. "I've seen this place; it's no fit country for real creatures. Everything is dead—no flesh or blood or growing thing anywhere."
paragraphs.zh: “一切,”吉姆抱怨道，“我见过这个地方；这根本不是真正生物该待的地方。这里的一切都是死气沉沉的——没有任何生机、血肉或生长的东西。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy replied, "We can't turn back and don't intend to stay there." Jim growled stubbornly, "It's dangerous." The Wizard interrupted, "Little Dorothy and I have been in many queer countries and always escaped harm.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西回答说：“我们不能回头，也不打算在那里停留。”吉姆固执地嘟囔道：“这很危险。”巫师插话说：“多萝西和我经历过许多古怪的国度，总是能够化险为夷。”

paragraphs.en: We've even been to the Land of Oz—haven't we, Dorothy? So we don't much care what the Country of the Gargoyles is like. Go ahead, Jim; whatever happens, we'll make the best of it."
paragraphs.zh: 我们甚至去过奥兹国——不是吗，多萝西？所以我们不太在乎石像怪所在的国家是什么样子。吉姆，你先去吧；不管发生什么，我们都得尽力而为。

paragraphs.en: "All right," answered Jim. "This is your excursion, and not mine. If you get into trouble, don't blame me."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”吉姆回答说，“这是你的郊游，不是我的。如果你遇到麻烦，可别怪我。”

paragraphs.en: Upon delivering his speech, he pushed forward and hauled the buggy up the remaining steps. Zeb exclaimed, "The Country of the Gargoyles is all wooden!" Indeed, the ground was sawdust, and pebbles scattered around were hard knots from trees, worn smooth over time.
paragraphs.zh: 发表完演讲后，他向前一冲，把马车拉上了最后几级台阶。泽布脱口而出：“木头怪兽国全是木头做的！”确实如此，地面是锯末，散落在四周的鹅卵石则是经过岁月打磨变得光滑的树结。

paragraphs.en: Wooden houses with carved flowers in front yards stood amidst tree trunks made of coarse wood, while leaves were shavings, and patches of grass were splintered wood. A solid wooden flooring covered areas where neither grass nor sawdust appeared.
paragraphs.zh: 前院雕刻着花朵的木屋矗立在粗制木头做成的树干之中，树叶是木屑，草地则是碎木片。没有草皮和锯末的地方铺着坚实的木地板。

paragraphs.en: Wooden birds fluttered among the trees, and wooden cows grazed on wooden grass. The most astonishing sight was the multitude of wooden people—Gargoyles. These creatures, less than three feet tall, had round bodies, short thick legs, and extraordinarily long arms.
paragraphs.zh: 树木间飞翔着木制的鸟儿，地上则有木制的牛在啃食着木制的草。最令人惊讶的是那些木制的人——石像鬼。这些小精灵身高不到三英尺，圆滚滚的身体，短粗的双腿，却有着异常修长的手臂。

paragraphs.en: Their heads were disproportionately large for their bodies, with faces that were decidedly ugly. Some had curved noses and wide grinning mouths, while others had flat noses, protruding eyes, and elephant-like ears. Despite the variety in appearance, all Gargoyles were equally disagreeable.
paragraphs.zh: 他们的头相对于身体来说异常大，面孔也相当难看。有的长着弯曲的鼻子和宽大的笑容，而另一些则有着扁平的鼻子、突出的眼睛以及象牙般的大耳朵。尽管它们在外貌上各不相同，但所有石像鬼都同样令人讨厌。

paragraphs.en: The tops of their heads lacked hair but bore carved designs—some with rows of points or balls, others resembling flowers or vegetables, and still others with waffle-like squares cut criss-cross. They wore short wooden wings attached to their bodies by wooden hinges and screws, which they used to fly swiftly and silently. Their legs were of little use for this purpose.
paragraphs.zh: 他们的头顶光秃秃的，却雕刻着各种图案——有的排列成行或圆点，有的像花朵或蔬菜，还有一些则像是被纵横切割开来的方格。他们身上装有短小的木制翅膀，由木质铰链和螺丝固定在身体上，可以让他们迅速而无声地飞翔。然而，这些腿对于飞行来说几乎派不上用场。

paragraphs.en: The Gargoyles' noiseless motion was peculiar; they made no sounds while flying or speaking, conversing instead through quick signals with their fingers or lips. The entire wooden country echoed with silence—no birds sang, nor did cows moo. Yet, there was more than ordinary activity everywhere.
paragraphs.zh: 木兽头的行动无声无息，他们在飞行或交谈时没有任何声响，而是通过快速的手势或唇语进行交流。整个木质国度一片寂静——没有鸟鸣，也没有牛叫。然而，这里的一切活动却异常频繁。

paragraphs.en: The group of strange creatures, clustered near the stairs, stared silently at the intruders with evil eyes. The Wizard and children, along with the horse and kitten, examined them equally intently.
paragraphs.zh: 这群奇怪的生物挤在楼梯附近，用充满恶意的眼神默默地盯着入侵者。巫师和孩子们，还有马匹和小猫，同样专注地打量着它们。

paragraphs.en: "Trouble is coming," said the horse. "Zeb, unhitch me from the buggy so I can fight."
paragraphs.zh: “麻烦来了，”马说道，“佐比，快把我从马车上解下来，我要去战斗。”

paragraphs.en: The Wizard agreed: "We must prepare for conflict. My sword isn't enough; I'll use my revolvers instead." He retrieved two deadly-looking revolvers from his satchel, causing the children to step back in alarm.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师同意道：“我们必须为战斗做好准备。我的剑不够用，我改用左轮手枪。”他从背包里取出两把看起来十分致命的左轮手枪，孩子们不禁退后了几步，显得有些惊慌。

paragraphs.en: "Dorothy," he said, "what harm could these Gargoyles do?"
paragraphs.zh: “多萝西，”他问道，“这些木制石像鬼能造成什么危害？”

paragraphs.en: "They have no weapons," she replied. "Their arms are just wooden clubs."
paragraphs.zh: “他们没有武器，”她回答，“他们的手臂只是木制的棒子。”

paragraphs.en: The Wizard warned: "Even with my guns, we can only damage a few of their bodies. After that, they'll be at our mercy."
paragraphs.zh: 巫师警告说：“即使有我的武器，也只能对他们造成有限的伤害。之后，他们就任由我们处置了。”

paragraphs.en: "Why fight then?" asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: “为什么要打呢？”多萝西问道。

paragraphs.en: "To die with a clear conscience," the Wizard replied gravely. "It's every man’s duty to do his best."
paragraphs.zh: “带着清白之心死去，”巫师庄重地回答，“每个人都有尽力而为的职责。”

paragraphs.en: Zeb, having unhitched the horse, wished for an axe. The Wizard noted they might have brought useful items if they had known about this adventure in advance.
paragraphs.zh: 泽布解开了马匹的缰绳，希望能有一把斧头。巫师注意到，如果他们提前知道这次冒险的话，或许会带上一些有用的东西。

paragraphs.en: The Gargoyles moved back when they heard talking but quickly advanced as soon as the conversation stopped. They flew toward the strangers with their long arms outstretched like sail-boats' bowsprits, focusing on the horse due to its size and strangeness.
paragraphs.zh: 当听到说话声时，石像鬼退后了一步，但一停下对话便迅速上前。他们伸长手臂飞向陌生人，仿佛帆船的船首柱一般，目光集中在那匹马身上，因为它体型庞大且显得格外不同寻常。

paragraphs.en: Jim was prepared for the Gargoyles. Seeing them approach, he turned his hooves towards them and kicked out with all his strength. The iron-shod hoofs struck the wooden bodies, causing splinters to fly as the Gargoyles scattered like straws in the wind.
paragraphs.zh: 吉姆早就预料到了这些石像鬼。见它们逼近，他猛地一转身，用全身的力量踢了出去。铁蹄重重地击打在木制的身体上，木屑四溅，石像鬼们如同随风飘散的稻草般四处飞散。

paragraphs.en: Despite their retreat, the Wizard remained unconvinced.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管他们退缩了，巫师仍不肯相信。

paragraphs.en: "Those wooden things are impossible to hurt," he said. "Jim's kicks only knocked a few splinters from their noses and ears. They won't look any uglier for it."
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“那些木头玩意儿伤不了。”“吉姆的踢击只能让他们鼻子和耳朵掉下几块碎屑，不会因此变得更丑陋。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy asked, "What made them fly away?"
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西问道：“是什么让他们飞走了？”

paragraphs.en: "The noise," replied the Wizard. "Remember how the Champion escaped by shouting his battle-cry?"
paragraphs.zh: “噪音，”巫师回答道，“你还记得冠军是如何通过喊出战斗口号逃脱的吗？”

paragraphs.en: The boy suggested, "We could escape down the stairs too. I'd rather face invisible bears than those wooden imps."
paragraphs.zh: 男孩提议说：“我们也可以从楼梯逃下去。与其面对看不见的熊，我宁愿对付那些木制的小妖精。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy firmly disagreed: "No, we can't go back. We need to fight it out."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西坚定地反对道：“不，我们不能回去。我们必须正面解决这个问题。”

paragraphs.en: The Wizard agreed, stating, "They haven't defeated us yet, and Jim is worth a whole army."
paragraphs.zh: 巫师同意了，说道：“他们还没有打败我们，而吉姆一个人顶得上一支大军。”

paragraphs.en: This time, the Gargoyles did not attack Jim directly. Joining in greater numbers, they flew over his head towards Dorothy and the others.
paragraphs.zh: 这次，石像鬼没有直接攻击吉姆。它们数量更多了，飞过他的头顶，朝多萝西和其他人扑去。

paragraphs.en: The Wizard raised his revolver and fired into the swarm of enemies. The shot echoed like thunder in the silent place. Some wooden beings fell to the ground, trembling; most managed to escape again.
paragraphs.zh: 巫师举起手枪，向敌人群中连开数枪。枪声在寂静的空间中回响，如同雷鸣一般。一些木制生物应声倒地，颤抖不已；大多数则侥幸逃走了。

paragraphs.en: Zeb ran to pick up one of the Gargoyles closest to him. The top of its head was carved into a crown, and a Wizard's bullet hit it in the left eye—a hard wooden knot. Half the bullet remained embedded in the wood, while half protruded.
paragraphs.zh: 泽布飞奔过去捡起离他最近的一个石像鬼。石像鬼的头顶雕刻成王冠的样子，一枚巫师的子弹正中它的左眼——那是一颗坚硬的木结。子弹嵌入木质的部分还有一半露在外面。

paragraphs.en: This jar from the impact had knocked the creature down more than any actual injury. Before the crowned Gargoyle could recover, Zeb tied several straps around its body to confine its wings and arms. He then securely fastened the creature and tossed it into the buggy.
paragraphs.zh: 这次撞击让怪兽摔了个跟头，比任何实质性伤害都更厉害。在加冕的石像鬼还没来得及恢复过来之前，泽布已经用几条皮带将其身体绑住，限制了它的翅膀和手臂。随后，他牢牢固定好这只怪兽，把它扔进了马车上。

paragraphs.en: By this time, the others had already retreated.
paragraphs.zh: 到这时，其他人已经退走了。
